title: dylan-park-private-deploy-scratchpad-2026-03-04
content:
Daily scratchpad - private deploy field notes (customer A)

Date: 2026-03-04 09:15am
Owner: Dylan Park
Context: Onsite/VPC install prep for Customer A (regulated finance). Doing a dry-run in staging with their network config. Notes to self and action items.

High level goal:
- Validate install path for Private (VPC) deployment into Customer A's AWS account + on-prem GPU nodes for heavy inference. Ensure KMS integration and audit logging meet compliance.

Preflight checklist (staging run observations):
- IAM roles: created cross-account role per Confluence template. Verified assume-role works from control plane account.
- VPC peering & route tables: staging VPC -> customer transit VPC peering established, but route table missing /30 route for bastion. Need ops to add the route (ticket to networking team).
- Subnets: public/private separation good. Confirmed NAT gateway in place for outbound image pulls.
- Security groups: opened 8443, 443, 22 for targets; still need to confirm if customer policy requires 9443 instead of 8443.
- KMS: test envelope encryption using customer KMS key succeeded for small file, but role needs kms:Decrypt on key policy (missing). Customer security to add principal.
- Certificates: customer uses internal CA - need cert upload flow working; test cert signed and uploaded to control plane succeeded once CA chain provided.
- DNS: Internal names resolve but TTLs long (12h) - for final rollout recommend TTL reduction for canary switch.
- NTP/time sync: one on-prem host skewed by ~7s - flagged (can break TLS). Ask customer to sync.
- Docker images: registry behind proxy - blob storage throttled; images pulled slower than expected. Add pre-pull step during maintenance window.
- CUDA/drivers: on one GPU node driver reported 470.x while runtime expects 525.x -> need ops to upgrade drivers or select compatible container runtime (fallback image available).
- SELinux/Firewall: Some hosts defaulted to enforcing; kernel param net.ipv4.ip_forward unset (required for overlay). Documented workaround: set sysctl and persist.
- Disk: /var/lib/docker low on space on host-03 (60% used but small disk); recommend increase or set overlay2 root to larger mount.
- Monitoring/agent: log shipper (fluentbit) failed due to proxy auth; need proxy credentials from customer or use sidecar with direct egress.

Install steps (rough draft for final runbook):
1) Preflight call with customer network/security (confirm KMS principal, proxy creds, CA chain, NTP).
2) Ensure IAM role + cross-account trust tested (assume-role from control plane).
3) Pre-pull images to all on-prem nodes (maintenance window).
4) Upgrade GPU drivers on nodes lacking required CUDA libs OR use CPU fallback for initial workloads.
5) Apply sysctl (net.ipv4.ip_forward=1) and ensure SELinux policies allow container runtime.
6) Upload TLS certs to control plane, verify chain and audit log entries.
7) Configure routing & LB: ensure routes for internal LB IPs and health-check ports (8443/9443), set TTL short for canary.
8) Start control-plane connectors, verify KV cache persists across restart, run smoke test (simple /generate prompt).
9) Enable metrics and trace hooks; validate token-level cost logs show up in Console.
10) Canary: route 5% traffic -> observe errors/latency for 2 hours, then 25%, then full.

Current blockers and action items:
- Blocker: customer KMS key policy missing kms:Decrypt for role -> ACTION: Samira to loop in customer security (PR sent).
- Blocker: network route for bastion /30 missing in transit VPC -> ACTION: Riley to open network ticket (N/W-404) and get ETA.
- Blocker: GPU driver mismatch on host-02/03 -> ACTION: Ops to schedule driver upgrade or we use fallback image; escalate if driver cannot be changed due to company policy.
- Blocker: registry proxy throttling causing image pull failures -> ACTION: request proxy creds or allow egress to our public registry for image pulls; file Jira PD-987.
- Follow-up: reduce DNS TTL to 300s before canary switch (ops + customer).

Quick reminders / notes to self:
- Keep canary window during low-traffic period (Customer A: 02:00-04:00 UTC).
- Bring fallback plan: route to hosted Redwood-verified model for 503s > 1% for 5m. Document rollback steps.
- Double-check logging retention settings to satisfy compliance (90 days required).
- Add smoke prompts covering sensitive PII redaction to canary tests.

Meeting notes (09:00 sync with customer):
- Customer security: will update KMS policy end-of-day.
- Network: will add route by tomorrow 17:00 PST.
- Ops: can schedule driver upgrade Friday maintenance window; confirmed pre-pull feasible.
- Customer asks for whitepaper on our on-prem keystore approach - Samira to provide.

To-do (priority):
- [ ] Confirm KMS policy changed (Samira)
- [ ] Network route ticket N/W-404 status (Riley)
- [ ] Schedule driver upgrade or pick fallback image (Ops)
- [ ] Pre-pull images during maintenance window (me + Ops)
- [ ] Prep rollback runbook and test in staging (me)
- [ ] Collect proxy credentials or arrange registry allowlist (Customer)
- [ ] Upload final cert chain to control plane (after CA chain received)

Notes for runbook improvement:
- Add explicit expected kernel params and SELinux exceptions per distro (Ubuntu 22.04 vs RHEL 8) - found differences during staging.
- Include exact list of TCP/UDP ports and health-check endpoints; customer firewall team asked for a single YAML of all ports.
- Add step to verify system time drift <2s before TLS handshake tests.

Random brain dump / risks:
- Risk: corporate proxies that MITM TLS may break our auth with customer KMS; test path for direct egress as fallback.
- Risk: heavy inference models can saturate NICs on 10Gb hosts if batching config wrong; include NIC monitoring thresholds in runbook.

End of notes.

-- Dylan
